intro: Each week has seven short days between classes. Day 1 is the day after class; Day 7 is class day. Every day has something to read, to think about, to pray and to do, about ten or fifteen minutes in all. Miss a day? Just pick up where you are.

remember.name: Look back
remember.about: The day after class: hold on to what you heard before it fades.

scripture.name: Scripture
scripture.about: A day to sit with the word of God and let it speak.

watch.name: Watch or listen
watch.about: A short video or podcast from a trusted Catholic teacher, with a summary for offline days.

reason.name: Think it through
reason.about: Faith and reason: a real question people ask, answered step by step.

story.name: A story
story.about: Someone who walked this road before you, and found Christ.

live.name: Live it
live.about: Faith you can do today, at home, at work, at the table.

class.name: Get ready for class
class.about: Class day: gather your questions and bring your week with you.

s01.title: Someone walks beside you
s01.think: In class you met two disciples walking away from Jerusalem, sad and confused. Jesus came and walked with them, but they did not know him. Faith often starts like this: God is already close before we can name him.
s01.journal: What first made you start walking toward the Church? Write it as a short story.
s01.pray: Lord Jesus, you walked with the two disciples before they knew it was you. Walk with me this week, and open my eyes a little more each day. Amen.
s01.do: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly three times today: when you wake, before a meal and before sleep. Say each word with attention.

s01.title: Did not our hearts burn?
s01.think: Jesus explained the Scriptures to them, "beginning at Moses and all the prophets." The whole Bible points to him. Their hearts burned while he spoke, long before they understood.
s01.journal: Has something about Jesus ever made your heart "burn"? What was it?
s01.pray: Jesus, speak to me through your word. Let my heart burn, and give me patience when I do not yet understand.
s01.do: Do this week's Bible study on the whole Emmaus story. It takes about fifteen minutes.

s01.title: Known in the breaking of the bread

media.by: Bishop Robert Barron, Word on Fire
media.title: Bishop Barron on the road to Emmaus
media.about: Bishop Barron has preached many times on Emmaus. He shows its pattern: Jesus finds us when we walk the wrong way, opens the Scriptures, and makes himself known in the breaking of the bread, which is the Mass. Choose one of his short Sunday sermons.
media.listen: the same pattern at every Mass: Jesus speaks in the readings, then gives himself in the Eucharist.

s01.think: The two ran back seven miles in the dark to tell the others. Meeting Jesus does not stay private. It sends us back to the community.
s01.journal: Who would you tell first if you became sure that Jesus is alive?
s01.pray: Jesus, you are alive. Make me a person who carries good news, not only one who hears it.
s01.do: Tell one person, gently, that you have started RCIA, or share one thing you learned in class.

s01.title: Doubts are welcome here

reason.q: Is it wrong to have doubts?
steps: The disciples on the road were full of doubt. Jesus did not send them away; he walked with them and gave them reasons from Scripture.
A question you cannot answer yet is not the same as refusing to believe. The Church calls honest searching "faith seeking understanding."
Faith is not believing without reasons. It is trusting someone worthy of trust, after looking at the evidence: the witnesses, history and changed lives.
So bring your doubts into the open. Truth has nothing to fear from an honest question.

s01.think: Thomas wanted proof, and Jesus gave it to him. Then he blessed those who would believe through the witness of others, which includes you.
s01.journal: Write your biggest question about faith, honestly, in one sentence.
s01.pray: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief. (Mark 9:24)
s01.do: Copy your question into "My questions for class" so you can ask it on Day 7.

s01.title: Take and read

story.name: St. Augustine of Hippo
story.text:
Augustine was born in North Africa in 354. He was brilliant and restless. He tried one philosophy after another and chased success and pleasure, while his mother Monica prayed for him for years.

In a garden in Milan, in 386, he wept because he could not change. Then he heard a child's voice singing, "Take and read." He opened Paul's letter and read: "Put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ." Peace filled his heart. He was baptized at the Easter Vigil the next spring, and became one of the greatest teachers of the Church.

s01.think: Augustine searched with his mind for years. His questions were not wasted: they brought him to the door.
s01.journal: Like Augustine, what is your heart restless for?
s01.pray: You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you. (St. Augustine)
s01.do: Find ten quiet minutes today with your phone in another room. Sit and tell God, "I am here."

s01.title: Stay with us, Lord
s01.think: The disciples begged the stranger, "Stay with us, because it is towards evening." Jesus let himself be invited in. At every Mass he is known again in the breaking of the bread.
s01.journal: When this week did the day feel like "evening," lonely or heavy?
s01.pray: Stay with us, Lord, for it is evening and the day is almost over. Stay in my home, my work and my heart.
s01.do: Go to Sunday Mass this week. Watch the moment the priest breaks the Host, and remember Emmaus.

s01.title: Bring your road to class
s01.class: Look back over the week. Write down anything you did not understand, or want to talk about. In RCIA there are no silly questions.
s01.think: The Good Shepherd walks with his sheep, even through the dark valley. Today you walk on with your class, your catechist and your sponsor.
s01.journal: What was your best moment with God this week?
s01.pray: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. Lead me, Lord, to the next step.
s01.do: Take the short review quiz, then read your questions once more before class.

s02.title: Made for God
s02.think: Paul told the thinkers of Athens that God made every nation "that they should seek God, if happily they may feel after him," for he is not far from any of us. The longing you feel is itself a clue.
s02.journal: Before RCIA, who did you think God was? Has that changed?
s02.pray: God, you are not far from me. In you I live and move and have my being. Let me know you as you really are.
s02.do: Pray the Glory Be three times today, slowly, once for the Father, once for the Son, once for the Holy Spirit.

s02.title: I AM WHO AM
s02.think: At the burning bush God gives Moses his name: "I AM WHO AM." God is not one thing among others in the world. He is being itself, the source of everything that exists, and yet he calls Moses by name.
s02.journal: God calls Moses by name. What would it mean for you that God knows your name?
s02.pray: Holy God, you are the one who simply is. Here I am, Lord. Speak, and teach me to listen.
s02.do: Take off your shoes for one minute of prayer, like Moses on holy ground, and simply say, "Here I am."

s02.title: Where is the evidence for God?

media.title: Where is the evidence for God?
media.about: A short, clear answer. Bishop Barron explains why God cannot be found like an object under a microscope: God is not one more thing in the universe but the reason anything exists at all. We come to know him through reason, beauty, conscience and his own revelation.
media.listen: why "Why is there something rather than nothing?" is a real question.

s02.think: Paul says God's "invisible things" are "clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made." Creation is like a signature. Reason can know that God exists; Jesus shows us who he is.
s02.journal: Where in nature or in people have you sensed something bigger than us?
s02.pray: Creator of all things, thank you for the world you made. Let everything beautiful I see today lead me to you.
s02.do: Go outside for ten minutes. Look closely at one thing (a tree, the sky, your hand) and thank God for it.

s02.title: Does God really exist?

reason.q: Can a thinking person believe in God?
steps: Everything we see depends on something else to exist: you on your parents, the earth on the sun, the sun on older stars.
A chain of things that all depend on something else cannot explain itself, however long it is. Something must exist that does not depend on anything.

That reality, existing by its own nature and giving existence to all else, is what people mean by God. Science studies how things work inside the universe; this question asks why there is a universe at all.
Add the order of nature, the moral law in your conscience and your longing for meaning, and belief in God is not a leap in the dark but the most reasonable answer.

s02.think: "The heavens shew forth the glory of God." The psalm says creation speaks without words. Reason and wonder work together.
s02.journal: Which reason for God makes the most sense to you? Which question still bothers you?
s02.pray: God, you gave me a mind to think. Let me use it honestly, and lead my thinking to you.
s02.do: Explain one of these steps in your own words to yourself, or to a friend who asks.

s02.title: A philosopher finds the truth

story.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein)
story.text:
Edith Stein grew up in a Jewish family in Germany, and as a teenager she stopped believing in God. She became one of the first women in Germany to earn a doctorate in philosophy, and she cared above all about truth.

In 1921, staying with friends, she picked up the life of St. Teresa of Avila and read it through the night. When she closed it she said, "This is the truth." She was baptized on New Year's Day 1922, later became a Carmelite nun, and died at Auschwitz in 1942, offering her life for her people.

s02.think: Edith searched for truth with all her intelligence, and when she found it she gave everything for it. Truth is not an idea; it is a Person.
s02.journal: What would you give up if you became sure something was true?
s02.pray: Lord, you promise, "You shall seek me, and shall find me, when you shall seek me with all your heart." Here is my heart.
s02.do: Read the page about St. Teresa Benedicta in the saints section, and ask her to pray for your search.

s02.title: God is love
s02.think: John does not say God has love, but that God is love. If God is love, then you were made out of love and for love, and every act of real love brings you closer to him.
s02.journal: Who has shown you what love looks like? Write a line of thanks for them.
s02.pray: God of love, you loved me first. Teach me to love the people you put in front of me today.
s02.do: Do one hidden kindness today that no one will thank you for.

s02.title: Questions about God
s02.class: What about God is still unclear or hard for you? Suffering, prayer, the Trinity, other religions? Write it down to ask.
s02.think: "My thoughts are not your thoughts." God is bigger than our minds, but his word does not return empty. Every honest question is a door.
s02.journal: In one sentence: who is God for you today?
s02.pray: Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Lord, I am seeking you.
s02.do: Read your notes from this week, and choose the one question you most want answered.

s03.title: Prayer is a conversation
s03.think: Jesus says: go into your room, close the door, and pray to your Father in secret. Prayer is not a performance or many words. It is talking with someone who already knows you and loves you.
s03.journal: What did you learn in class about prayer that surprised you?
s03.pray: Father, here I am, in secret, with you. I don't know how to pray well, but I want to be with you.
s03.do: Choose your "inner room" for this week: one chair, one corner, one time each day for prayer.

s03.title: Ask, seek, knock
s03.think: Jesus uses three verbs, each stronger than the last. And he gives the reason: if human parents give good things to their children, how much more will your Father in heaven.
s03.journal: What are you asking God for right now? Write it plainly.
s03.pray: Father, I ask, I seek, I knock. Give me what is good for me, even when it is not what I expected.
s03.do: Do this week's Bible study on the Our Father (Matthew 6:5-15).

s03.title: Praying with your imagination

media.title: Praying Like This Changed My Life
media.about: Fr. Mike explains a way of praying taught by St. Ignatius: read a Gospel scene, then step into it with your imagination. Where are you standing? What do you hear? What does Jesus say to you?
media.listen: the simple steps, so you can try them with today's reading.

s03.think: Bartimaeus is blind, poor and loud. People tell him to be quiet. Jesus stops and asks, "What wilt thou that I should do to thee?" He asks you the same.
s03.journal: If Jesus asked you, "What do you want me to do for you?", what would you say?
s03.pray: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me. Lord, that I may see.
s03.do: Pray with today's Gospel the way the video shows: read it twice, then imagine yourself on the roadside.

s03.title: When God seems silent

reason.q: Why pray if God already knows everything, or if he seems not to answer?
steps: Prayer is not giving God information. It is a relationship, and relationships need time together, even when little is said.
Good parents do not give a child everything immediately. "Not yet" and "I have something better" are also answers.
Prayer changes the one who prays. Over time it shapes what we desire, so we start to want what is truly good.
Jesus himself prayed and felt God's silence on the cross, and the Father answered with the Resurrection. Silence is not absence.

s03.think: Jesus told this parable "that we ought always to pray, and not to faint." Keep coming back, like the widow at the judge's door.
s03.journal: Has a prayer of yours been answered in a way you did not expect?
s03.pray: Lord, when you seem silent, help me to stay. I would rather sit with you in silence than talk without you.
s03.do: Pray for five minutes today without asking for anything: just thank God and stay quiet with him.

s03.title: The porter of Mount Royal

story.name: St. André Bessette
story.text:
Alfred Bessette was born in Quebec in 1845, sickly and barely able to read. The Holy Cross brothers almost refused him. They made him the doorkeeper of their school in Montreal, and he stayed at that door for forty years.

Brother André spent his nights in prayer and his days listening to the sick and the poor. He told them to pray to St. Joseph, and many were healed. "I am only a little dog of St. Joseph," he said. From his small chapel grew Saint Joseph's Oratory on Mount Royal, where people from all over the world still come to pray.

s03.think: Jesus thanks the Father for revealing himself "to the little ones." You do not need to be clever or important to pray. Brother André just kept the door and kept praying.
s03.journal: Where is your "door", the ordinary place where you could pray every day?
s03.pray: St. Joseph, you cared for Jesus and Mary. Care for me too, and teach me to pray with a simple heart.
s03.do: Say a short prayer each time you open a door today: "Jesus, I trust in you."

s03.title: Pray at the table
s03.think: "The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord: and thou givest them meat in due season." Thanking God before meals is one of the easiest ways to pray every day.
s03.journal: What are three things you are grateful for today?
s03.pray: Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord. Amen.
s03.do: Say grace before every meal today, even in a restaurant or at work. A quiet Sign of the Cross is enough.

s03.title: Bring your prayer to class
s03.class: What is hard for you about prayer: finding time, distractions, not feeling anything, not knowing what to say? Write it down to ask.
s03.think: The disciples asked, "Lord, teach us to pray." That is still the best prayer for a beginner, and for a saint.
s03.journal: How did your prayer change this week, even a little?
s03.pray: Lord, teach me to pray. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.
s03.do: Take the review quiz and practise the Our Father by heart.

sym1-01.title: One God, three Persons
sym1-01.think: Jesus sends his friends to baptize "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." One name, three Persons. Christians did not invent the Trinity; they met it in Jesus.
sym1-01.journal: What helped you most in class to understand the Trinity a little?
sym1-01.pray: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be. Amen.
sym1-01.do: Each time you make the Sign of the Cross today, notice the three names and the one cross.

sym1-01.title: The Father, the Son and the Spirit at the Jordan
sym1-01.think: At Jesus' baptism all three appear: the Son in the water, the Spirit like a dove, the Father's voice: "This is my beloved Son." At your baptism the Father will say the same to you.
sym1-01.journal: How does it feel to imagine God saying to you, "You are my beloved"?
sym1-01.pray: Father, let me hear your voice. Jesus, let me follow you into the water. Holy Spirit, come upon me.
sym1-01.do: Do this week's Bible study on Matthew 28:16-20.

sym1-01.title: A God who is relationship

media.title: Fr. Mike on the Trinity
media.about: Ascension Presents has several short videos where Fr. Mike explains the Trinity and why it matters for everyday life: God is not lonely. From all eternity he is a communion of love, and he invites us into it.
media.listen: why "God is love" only makes full sense if God is three Persons.

sym1-01.think: Jesus prays that we may be one "as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee." The Trinity is not a math problem; it is the family of love we are invited to join.
sym1-01.journal: Where do you see a small picture of the Trinity's love in your life (a family, a friendship)?
sym1-01.pray: Holy Trinity, one God, make your home in me. Let me share the love you have among yourselves.
sym1-01.do: Call or message someone you love today, just to tell them you are glad they exist.

sym1-01.title: Is one plus one plus one three?

reason.q: Do Christians believe in three gods?
steps: No. Christians believe in one God, as strongly as Jews and Muslims do. "Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord."
The Trinity does not say one god equals three gods. It says one divine nature (what God is) is shared fully by three Persons (who God is): Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Think of how you know yourself and love yourself while staying one person. In God, his perfect Word and his perfect Love are so full that they are Persons, yet not separate beings.
We did not reason our way to this; God revealed it in Jesus. But it is not a contradiction: it would be one only if we said one and three in the same sense.

sym1-01.think: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." With God, and God: John holds both together.
sym1-01.journal: How would you explain to a friend that Christians worship one God?
sym1-01.pray: O God, you are one and you are love. I adore you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
sym1-01.do: Read the Apostles' Creed slowly and notice its three parts: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

sym1-01.title: A seeker meets an old man by the sea

story.name: St. Justin Martyr
story.text:
Justin was born around the year 100 in Samaria, to a pagan family. He wanted to know the truth about God, so he went from teacher to teacher: a Stoic, a follower of Aristotle, a Pythagorean, a Platonist. Each left him hungry.

One day, walking alone by the sea, he met an old man who told him about the prophets and about Christ. "A fire was kindled in my soul," Justin wrote. He became a Christian and kept wearing his philosopher's cloak, because he had found "the only sure and useful philosophy." He taught in Rome and was martyred there around 165.

sym1-01.think: Justin did not stop thinking when he believed. Faith gave his reason a home.
sym1-01.journal: Which "teachers" (ideas, books, people) have you tried in your search for meaning?
sym1-01.pray: Lord, kindle a fire in my soul. Let my mind and my heart both find their rest in you.
sym1-01.do: Write down one thing you still want to understand about God, and one thing you already trust.

sym1-01.title: Faith is a gift and a choice
sym1-01.think: Abraham "went out, not knowing whither he went." Faith is God's gift, and also our free yes. It is like Abraham packing his bags: trust that moves your feet.
sym1-01.journal: What small step of trust is God asking of you right now?
sym1-01.pray: O my God, I firmly believe that you are one God in three divine Persons. Increase my faith.
sym1-01.do: Learn the Act of Faith this week. Today, just read it once aloud.

sym1-01.title: Bring your questions about faith
sym1-01.class: What about the Trinity, or about faith itself, is still confusing? Write it down. Your catechist has heard every question before.
sym1-01.think: Paul ends a letter with a blessing the priest still uses at Mass: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit.
sym1-01.journal: In your own words: why does it matter that God is a Trinity of love?
sym1-01.pray: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with me, and with all my class.
sym1-01.do: Take the review quiz, then listen for this blessing at the start of Sunday Mass.

sym1-02.title: God comes looking for us
sym1-02.think: In every other story people search for God. In the Bible, God searches for us, like a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one. That is what revelation means: God showing himself.
sym1-02.journal: Looking back, how has God come looking for you?
sym1-02.pray: Good Shepherd, you came looking for me. Thank you for not giving up. Carry me home on your shoulders.
sym1-02.do: Tell God three ways you see now that he has been leading you.

sym1-02.title: God has spoken by his Son
sym1-02.think: God spoke "at sundry times and in divers manners" through the prophets, and "last of all" in his Son. Jesus is God's final, complete Word. Everything else points to him.
sym1-02.journal: If Jesus is God's clearest Word, what is he saying to you this week?
sym1-02.pray: Jesus, Word of the Father, I want to hear you. Speak, Lord, your servant is listening.

sym1-02.title: To know and love God

media.by: Fr. Mike Schmitz, The Catechism in a Year
media.title: Day 1: To Know and Love God
media.about: The first episode of a free podcast that reads the whole Catechism in 365 short episodes. Fr. Mike explains why God made us: to share his own blessed life. A good way to start the habit of learning a little every day.
media.listen: the idea that God "calls" every person, at every time and place.

sym1-02.think: "Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me." God knows us completely, and he still wants to be known by us.
sym1-02.journal: Which line of Psalm 139 speaks to you most today?
sym1-02.pray: Search me, O God, and know my heart. Lead me in the way everlasting.
sym1-02.do: Listen to the episode on a walk or while cooking.

sym1-02.title: Can we trust the Bible?

reason.q: How do we know the Gospels are reliable?
steps: Luke says he wrote after carefully checking what "eyewitnesses" handed on. The Gospels were written within the lifetime of people who knew Jesus.
We have far more ancient copies of the New Testament (over 5,000 in Greek) than of any other ancient book, so we can be confident about what was first written.
The witnesses had nothing to gain: most of the apostles were killed for what they said they saw. People do not die for what they know is a lie.
And the Bible did not fall from the sky alone: the living Church that wrote it down also handed it on and still explains it. Scripture and Tradition belong together.

sym1-02.think: Luke wrote "that thou mayest know the verity of those words in which thou hast been instructed." The Gospel is meant to give you certainty, not just good feelings.
sym1-02.journal: What makes it hard, or easy, for you to trust what the Bible says?
sym1-02.pray: Lord, give me a mind that asks good questions and a heart that welcomes the truth.
sym1-02.do: Read the opening of Luke's Gospel (Luke 1:1-4) and his last chapter (24). Notice how he names real places and people.

sym1-02.title: Wise men from Persia

story.name: The Magi
story.text:
Matthew tells of "wise men from the east" who followed a star to Bethlehem. Early Christian art in Rome and Ravenna shows them in Persian dress, with soft caps and trousers, and an old tradition says the church of the Nativity in Bethlehem was spared by Persian soldiers in 614 because they saw their own ancestors pictured over the door.

They were scholars who watched the sky. God spoke to them in the language they knew, a star, and then led them further by the Scriptures that pointed to Bethlehem. They knelt before a child and gave him gold, frankincense and myrrh, then went home another way.

sym1-02.think: God reached the Magi through what they already loved, then completed it with his revealed word. He meets each of us where we are, and leads us further.
sym1-02.journal: What was your "star", the first sign that drew you toward Christ?
sym1-02.pray: Lord, you led the Magi by a star. Lead me too, and let me kneel before you with all I have.
sym1-02.do: Look at the night sky tonight, if you can, and pray for everyone still searching for God.

sym1-02.title: Treasure the word in your heart
sym1-02.think: "Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart." Revelation is not only information. It is something to keep and turn over, the way Mary did, until it shapes your life.
sym1-02.journal: Write down one word or line from this week that you want to keep.
sym1-02.pray: Mary, you kept God's word in your heart. Help me to keep it too, and to live it.
sym1-02.do: Write this week's memory verse on a card and keep it in your pocket or on your phone's lock screen.

sym1-02.title: Questions about the Bible and the Church
sym1-02.class: What do you want to understand about Scripture, Tradition and the Church's teaching? Why both, and not the Bible alone? Write it down.
sym1-02.think: Paul tells the Christians to hold the traditions they learned "whether by word, or by our epistle." Spoken and written, together.
sym1-02.journal: What did you learn this week about how God speaks?
sym1-02.pray: Lord, thank you for speaking to us through your word, your Church and your Spirit. Make me faithful to what I receive.
sym1-02.do: Take the review quiz, and bring your Bible to class if you have one.

sym1-03.title: A love letter, not a rulebook
sym1-03.think: Paul says all Scripture is "inspired of God": breathed out by him. The Bible is many books written over a thousand years by human authors, yet one Author speaks through all of them.
sym1-03.journal: What surprised you in class about how the Bible was written?
sym1-03.pray: Holy Spirit, you inspired the Scriptures. Open my mind to understand them and my heart to love them.
sym1-03.do: Find a Bible at home or in the app, and learn where the Gospels are: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

sym1-03.title: A lamp to my feet
sym1-03.think: "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths." A lamp does not show the whole road, only the next step. That is enough to walk.
sym1-03.journal: What is the next step you need light for?
sym1-03.pray: Lord, your word is a lamp to my feet. Show me my next step, and give me courage to take it.
sym1-03.do: Do this week's Bible study on 2 Timothy 3:14-17.

sym1-03.title: The whole story in ten minutes

media.by: Fr. Mike Schmitz, The Bible in a Year
media.title: The Bible in 10 Minutes
media.about: Fr. Mike walks through the big story of the Bible from creation to Jesus, so the 73 books stop feeling like a pile and start feeling like one story: God making a family, losing it to sin, and gathering it back.
media.listen: where you are in that story today.

sym1-03.think: Jesus opened their minds to understand that everything in "the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms" was about him. Read the Old Testament with Jesus in mind.
sym1-03.journal: Which part of the Bible's big story are you most curious about?
sym1-03.pray: Jesus, open my mind as you opened theirs, so I can see you on every page.
sym1-03.do: Look at the Bible study section's "Start here" guide, five minutes on how Catholics read the Bible.

sym1-03.title: The hard parts of the Bible

reason.q: What about violent or strange passages in the Bible?
steps: The Bible is a library, not one book. It holds history, poetry, law, prophecy and letters, and each must be read as what it is.
God taught his people step by step, like a teacher with children. Early stages were not the final word; Jesus is.
So Catholics read every passage in light of Christ and of the whole Bible, and with the Church, not alone. A hard verse is never read as permission to hate.
The Bible is honest about human sin, even the sins of its heroes. That honesty is a reason to trust it.

sym1-03.think: "The word of God is living and effectual." Some passages will puzzle you. Keep them as questions; they are part of the conversation.
sym1-03.journal: Is there a Bible passage that troubles you? Write it down to ask about.
sym1-03.pray: Lord, when I do not understand your word, keep me humble and keep me asking.
sym1-03.do: Write your question about a hard passage in "My questions for class."

sym1-03.title: Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ

story.name: St. Jerome
story.text:
Jerome was born around 347 in what is now Croatia. As a young student in Rome he loved Latin literature and found the Bible clumsy. Later, sick and feverish, he dreamed he stood before Christ the Judge, who told him, "You are a follower of Cicero, not of Christ."

He changed his life. He learned Hebrew from a Jewish teacher and moved to Bethlehem, where for decades he translated the Bible into the everyday Latin of his time. That translation, the Vulgate, was read in the Church for 1,500 years. His famous line: "Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ."

sym1-03.think: When Ezra read the law aloud, the people wept, then rejoiced "for the joy of the Lord is our strength." God's word, understood, brings joy.
sym1-03.journal: What would help you read the Bible more: a time, a place, a plan, a friend?
sym1-03.pray: St. Jerome, pray for me, that I may come to know Christ through his word.
sym1-03.do: Choose a Bible reading plan in the app and read Day 1 today.

sym1-03.title: Pray with a Gospel
sym1-03.think: Two disciples follow Jesus, and he turns and asks, "What seek you?" They answer with a question, and he says, "Come and see." Reading the Gospel is coming to see where he lives.
sym1-03.journal: What are you seeking? Answer Jesus' question in one line.
sym1-03.pray: Jesus, I want to come and see. Show me where you live, and let me stay with you today.
sym1-03.do: Pray with this Sunday's Gospel using Lectio Divina: read, reflect, respond, rest.

sym1-03.title: Bring your Bible questions
sym1-03.class: What do you want to ask about the Bible: how to start reading it, which translation to use, why Catholic Bibles have 73 books?
sym1-03.think: "The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen: but the word of our Lord endureth for ever." Everything else changes; God's word stays.
sym1-03.journal: Which verse from this week will you remember?
sym1-03.pray: Lord, your word lasts for ever. Plant it deep in me.
sym1-03.do: Take the review quiz and practise the memory verse with the flashcards.

sym1-04.title: Very good
sym1-04.think: The story begins with goodness, not sin. God makes everything and calls it good, and the human being "very good," made in his image. Whatever has gone wrong, this is who you are first.
sym1-04.journal: Creation, Fall, Redemption: which of the three words speaks to you most right now? Why?
sym1-04.pray: Creator God, you made me in your image and called me very good. Help me to see myself and others the way you see us.
sym1-04.do: Look in the mirror today and say, "I am made in the image of God." Then say it about someone who annoys you.

sym1-04.title: Where art thou?
sym1-04.think: After the first sin, Adam and Eve hide. But God comes walking in the garden and calls, "Where art thou?" Even here, God is the one who searches. And he promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent.
sym1-04.journal: Where are you hiding from God? Be honest; he already knows.
sym1-04.pray: Lord, you call me even when I hide. Here I am. I do not want to hide from you any more.
sym1-04.do: Do this week's Bible study on Genesis 3.

sym1-04.title: What went wrong with us?

media.by: Bishop Robert Barron, Word on Fire
media.title: Bishop Barron on original sin
media.about: Bishop Barron explains original sin not as a stain we inherit by bad luck but as a broken relationship that spreads, like a crack in a family. Everyone can see it in the world; the Gospel says it is not the last word.
media.listen: why grasping at being "like God" on our own terms is the root of sin.

sym1-04.think: Paul compares two men: through Adam, sin and death came in; through Jesus, grace overflows even more. The story of the Fall is told so that we long for the Redeemer.
sym1-04.journal: Where do you see brokenness in the world, or in yourself, that you cannot fix alone?
sym1-04.pray: Jesus, new Adam, where sin grew, let your grace overflow in me.
sym1-04.do: Watch one video, or read the summary, and then read Romans 5:20 again: "where sin abounded, grace did more abound."

sym1-04.title: If God is good, why is there evil?

reason.q: How can a good and powerful God allow suffering?
steps: God made us able to love, and love needs freedom. Freedom means we can also refuse, and much suffering comes from human choices.
Our sense that evil is wrong is itself a clue. If there were no God and no real good, suffering would just be how things are, not something unjust.
A God beyond us can have reasons we cannot see, as a parent allows a child a painful vaccine. Not seeing a reason is not proof that there is none.
Christianity does not explain suffering away. God entered it in Jesus, suffered with us on the cross, and promised that it ends in resurrection.

sym1-04.think: Paul says creation "groaneth and travaileth in pain," like a woman giving birth: suffering is real, but it is labour toward something new.
sym1-04.journal: What suffering in your life or in the world makes it hardest to believe?
sym1-04.pray: Lord, I bring you the suffering I do not understand. Stay with me in it, and give me hope.
sym1-04.do: Pray today for one person you know who is suffering, by name.

sym1-04.title: Sold as a slave, set free by Christ

story.name: St. Josephine Bakhita
story.text:
Bakhita was born in Darfur, Sudan, around 1869. When she was about seven, slave traders kidnapped her. The shock was so great that she forgot her own name; "Bakhita," meaning "lucky," was the name they gave her. She was sold several times and beaten often.

In Italy, with the Canossian Sisters, she learned of a God who had known her and loved her all along. "I am definitively loved, and whatever happens to me, I am awaited by this Love," she later said. She was baptized in 1890, became a sister, and was known for her gentleness and her forgiveness of those who hurt her.

sym1-04.think: "I have called thee by thy name: thou art mine." Bakhita lost her name, but God never forgot it. Redemption means being bought back and brought home.
sym1-04.journal: What would change if you truly believed, "I am definitively loved"?
sym1-04.pray: St. Josephine Bakhita, pray for all who are enslaved or abused today, and for me, that I may know I am loved.
sym1-04.do: Learn one fact about human trafficking in Canada, and pray for its victims.

sym1-04.title: Say sorry, to God and to someone
sym1-04.think: The younger son "came to himself," got up and went home. The father ran to meet him before he finished his speech. Turning back is always possible, and always welcomed.
sym1-04.journal: Is there someone you need to forgive, or ask forgiveness from?
sym1-04.pray: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended you. I firmly resolve, with the help of your grace, to sin no more.
sym1-04.do: Say sorry to one person today for something real, without excuses.

sym1-04.title: Questions about sin and salvation
sym1-04.class: What do you want to ask about creation, evolution, Adam and Eve, sin or salvation? Write it down.
sym1-04.think: "God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son." The whole story of salvation fits in this one verse.
sym1-04.journal: Write John 3:16 in your own words, with your own name in it.
sym1-04.pray: O my God, relying on your infinite goodness and promises, I hope to obtain pardon of my sins, the help of your grace, and life everlasting.
sym1-04.do: Take the review quiz, and say this week's memory verse from memory.

sym1-05.title: Who do you say that I am?
sym1-05.think: Jesus asks what people say about him, then makes it personal: "But whom do you say that I am?" Everyone has an opinion about Jesus. RCIA asks for your own answer.
sym1-05.journal: Who did you think Jesus was before? Who do you say he is today?
sym1-05.pray: Jesus, you are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Let this be my answer, not only Peter's.
sym1-05.do: Say the name of Jesus slowly and lovingly three times today, as a prayer.

sym1-05.title: The Word was made flesh
sym1-05.think: The Word who "was God" became flesh and "dwelt among us." God did not send a message from far away; he came himself, with a body, a mother, a hometown and a trade.
sym1-05.journal: What does it mean to you that God became a human being?
sym1-05.pray: Jesus, true God and true man, you came close to me. Help me to come close to you.
sym1-05.do: Do this week's Bible study on Matthew 16:13-20.

sym1-05.title: The identity of Jesus

media.title: The Identity of Jesus (SEEK 2021)
media.about: A talk to young adults. Bishop Barron shows that Jesus spoke and acted as only God could: he forgave sins, claimed authority over the Law and the Temple, and said, "Before Abraham was, I am." Either he was who he said, or he was not good at all.
media.listen: the claims of Jesus that no prophet ever made.

sym1-05.think: Jesus says to a paralysed man, "Thy sins are forgiven," and the scribes think: "Who can forgive sins, but God only?" They were right about that. Then he heals the man to show his authority.
sym1-05.journal: Which thing Jesus said or did makes you think he must be more than a prophet?
sym1-05.pray: Lord Jesus, you have authority to forgive and to heal. I bring you what needs forgiving and healing in me.
sym1-05.do: Watch the first fifteen minutes today and the rest another day, or read the summary.

sym1-05.title: Only a prophet?

reason.q: Was Jesus only a great prophet or teacher?
steps: Many respect Jesus as a prophet. But prophets said, "Thus says the Lord." Jesus said, "I say to you," forgave sins himself, and accepted worship.
He said, "Before Abraham was made, I am," using God's own name, and his hearers picked up stones because they understood exactly what he claimed.

A man who claims to be God is either lying, deluded, or telling the truth. A liar or a madman is not a great moral teacher. So "just a good teacher" is the one option the evidence does not leave open.
His life, his wisdom, his death and his Resurrection, witnessed by many, point to the third: he is who he said he is.

sym1-05.think: This is the heart of the Christian faith, and the hardest step for many. Take your time; Jesus is patient with honest seekers.
sym1-05.journal: What would it mean for your life if Jesus really is God?
sym1-05.pray: Jesus, if you are who you say, show me, and give me the courage to follow you.
sym1-05.do: Read one whole Gospel chapter today and notice what Jesus says about himself.

sym1-05.title: Knocked off his horse

story.name: St. Paul
story.text:
Saul was a brilliant, devout Jew who thought the followers of Jesus were dangerous. He watched Stephen being stoned and then set out for Damascus with letters to arrest Christians.

On the road a light from heaven threw him to the ground, and a voice said, "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" "Who art thou, Lord?" "I am Jesus whom thou persecutest." Blind for three days, he was baptized by Ananias, a Christian he had come to arrest. Saul became Paul, the apostle who carried the Gospel across the Roman world, and was martyred in Rome.

sym1-05.think: Jesus said, "why persecutest thou me?" not "my followers." Jesus and his Church are one. And no one is too far away for him to reach.
sym1-05.journal: Is there someone you think could never come to faith? Pray for them by name.
sym1-05.pray: Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? Open my eyes as you opened Paul's.
sym1-05.do: Add one person who seems far from God to your prayer list.

sym1-05.title: The way, the truth and the life
sym1-05.think: Thomas says, "we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" Jesus does not hand him a map. He says, "I am the way." Following Jesus is a friendship, not a set of directions.
sym1-05.journal: Where do you need Jesus to be "the way" for you this week?
sym1-05.pray: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, I place all my trust in you.
sym1-05.do: Before one decision today, small or big, pause and ask, "Jesus, what would you do?"

sym1-05.title: Bring your questions about Jesus
sym1-05.class: What still puzzles you about Jesus: how he can be God and man, what Christians believe compared with other religions, the history? Write it down.
sym1-05.think: He "emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." The God who made the stars knelt to wash feet and died on a cross. That is who Jesus is.
sym1-05.journal: Write one sentence to Jesus, telling him who he is for you right now.
sym1-05.pray: Every knee shall bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
sym1-05.do: Take the review quiz, and pray the Nicene Creed slowly, noticing everything it says about Jesus.

sym1-06.title: Greater love than this
sym1-06.think: "Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends." The Paschal Mystery is Jesus' passing over through death to life, and he calls you his friend.
sym1-06.journal: What struck you most in class about the cross and Resurrection?
sym1-06.pray: Jesus, you call me your friend. Thank you for laying down your life for me.
sym1-06.do: Look at a crucifix today for one full minute in silence.

sym1-06.title: It is consummated
sym1-06.think: At the foot of the cross stand his mother and the beloved disciple. Jesus gives them to each other, and then says, "It is consummated." The work of love is finished, completely.
sym1-06.journal: If you stood at the foot of the cross, what would you want to say to Jesus?
sym1-06.pray: We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy cross you have redeemed the world.
sym1-06.do: Do this week's Bible study on John 19:16-30.

sym1-06.title: Why did Jesus die the way he did?

media.title: Why Did Jesus Have to Die the Way He Did?
media.about: A short clip. Bishop Barron explains that on the cross Jesus took all the world's sin, violence and hatred into himself, and answered it not with more violence but with forgiveness. The cross shows what sin does and what God's love does.
media.listen: "Father, forgive them" as the answer to the world's violence.

sym1-06.think: Isaiah wrote seven centuries before Jesus: "he was wounded for our iniquities... and by his bruises we are healed." The early Christians read this and saw Good Friday.
sym1-06.journal: What wound in you do you want Jesus to heal?
sym1-06.pray: Lord Jesus, by your wounds I am healed. I give you my hurts and my sins.
sym1-06.do: Pray the Stations of the Cross in the app, or just the first three stations today.

sym1-06.title: Did the Resurrection really happen?

reason.q: Is there good reason to believe Jesus rose from the dead?
steps: Even sceptical historians agree on a few facts: Jesus died by crucifixion, his tomb was found empty, and many people said they saw him alive afterwards.
Paul lists witnesses, including "more than five hundred brethren at once," most still alive when he wrote, as if to say: go and ask them.
The disciples went from hiding in fear to facing prison and death. Something changed them; they said it was meeting the risen Jesus.
Other explanations (a stolen body, hallucinations, a legend) each fail to fit all the facts. The Resurrection does.

sym1-06.think: Paul hands on what he "received": Christ died, was buried, rose, and appeared. This is one of the oldest Christian creeds, written within a few years of the events.
sym1-06.journal: Which of these reasons is strongest for you? What would you still ask?
sym1-06.pray: Risen Jesus, if you are alive, let me meet you, as Mary Magdalene and the disciples did.
sym1-06.do: Explain to yourself, in three sentences, why the empty tomb matters.

sym1-06.title: A life for a life

story.name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
story.text:
Maximilian Kolbe was a Polish Franciscan priest who ran a large Catholic printing house. In 1941 the Nazis sent him to Auschwitz. When a prisoner escaped, the guards chose ten men to starve to death in a bunker.

One of them, Franciszek Gajowniczek, cried out, "My wife, my children!" Father Kolbe stepped forward and said, "I am a Catholic priest. I want to take his place." In the bunker he led the others in prayer and hymns until the end. Gajowniczek survived the war and lived to see Kolbe declared a saint in 1982.

sym1-06.think: "Unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, itself remaineth alone." Kolbe's death bore fruit, because Jesus' death had first.
sym1-06.journal: What small "dying to self" could you offer for someone else this week?
sym1-06.pray: St. Maximilian Kolbe, pray for me, that I may love as generously as you did.
sym1-06.do: Give up your place, your choice or your comfort for someone today, quietly.

sym1-06.title: Offer it up
sym1-06.think: Paul says he rejoices in his sufferings, filling up in his flesh "those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ." Joined to Jesus, even our small pains can become love for others.
sym1-06.journal: What is hard in your life right now that you could offer to God?
sym1-06.pray: O Jesus, it is for love of you, for the conversion of sinners, and in reparation for sin, that I offer this.
sym1-06.do: The next time something annoys or hurts today, say this short prayer instead of complaining.

sym1-06.title: Bring your questions about the cross
sym1-06.class: What do you still want to understand: why the cross was necessary, what the Resurrection means for us, what "saved" means? Write it down.
sym1-06.think: "Why seek you the living with the dead? He is not here, but is risen." The story does not end at the tomb.
sym1-06.journal: How does the Resurrection change the way you look at death?
sym1-06.pray: Soul of Christ, sanctify me. Body of Christ, save me. Within your wounds hide me.

sym1-07.title: God's life poured into you
sym1-07.think: "The charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us." Grace is not a thing; it is God's own life, given freely, making us his children.
sym1-07.journal: What did you learn in class about the Holy Spirit that was new to you?
sym1-07.pray: Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart and kindle in me the fire of your love.
sym1-07.do: Pray "Come, Holy Spirit" before you start work or study today.

sym1-07.title: Tongues of fire
sym1-07.think: At Pentecost the Spirit comes like wind and fire, and frightened disciples speak boldly in many languages. Among the crowd were "Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites": people from Persia heard the Gospel on the Church's first day.
sym1-07.journal: Where do you need courage that only the Holy Spirit can give?
sym1-07.pray: Holy Spirit, come upon me as you came on the apostles. Make me brave and joyful.
sym1-07.do: Do this week's Bible study on Acts 2:1-13.

sym1-07.title: Who is the Holy Spirit?

media.title: Fr. Mike on the Holy Spirit
media.about: Short videos where Fr. Mike explains that the Holy Spirit is not a force or a feeling but a Person, God himself, who lives in us after Baptism and Confirmation and gives us the strength to live like Jesus.
media.listen: how the Spirit works even when we feel nothing.

sym1-07.think: Jesus promises "another Paraclete," a helper, "that he may abide with you for ever." You are not left alone to be good by your own effort.
sym1-07.journal: Where in your life do you most need a helper right now?
sym1-07.pray: Spirit of truth, live in me. Help me where I am weak.
sym1-07.do: Write down the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety and fear of the Lord. Circle the one you most need.

sym1-07.title: Do miracles still happen?

reason.q: Isn't belief in miracles unscientific?
steps: Science studies how nature normally behaves. It cannot prove that nothing outside nature exists; that is a philosophical claim, not a scientific result.
If God made nature, he is free to act in it, the way an author can write a surprising chapter in his own book.
The Church is careful: before a healing is called a miracle (for example at Lourdes, or for a saint's canonization), doctors must confirm it has no natural explanation.
The greatest miracle is quieter: grace changing a human heart. Many people can tell you about that one.

sym1-07.think: Peter has no money, but says, "what I have, I give thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise, and walk." The Spirit works through ordinary people.
sym1-07.journal: Have you seen God change someone's heart, or your own?
sym1-07.pray: Lord, I believe you can do all things. Do in me whatever you want.
sym1-07.do: Ask someone in your parish or class how they came to faith. Listen for the Spirit's work.

sym1-07.title: From denial to Pentecost

story.name: St. Peter
story.text:
Peter was a fisherman, loyal and impulsive. He promised Jesus, "I will lay down my life for thee." That same night, by a fire in the high priest's courtyard, a servant girl asked if he knew Jesus, and three times he swore he did not. Then the cock crowed, and Peter went out and wept bitterly.

Fifty days later, filled with the Holy Spirit, the same man stood up before thousands in Jerusalem and proclaimed that Jesus is Lord and Christ. About three thousand were baptized that day. Peter led the Church, and at the end gave his life in Rome.

sym1-07.think: The difference between Peter at the fire and Peter at Pentecost was not willpower. It was the Holy Spirit.
sym1-07.journal: Where have you failed, and where might the Spirit want to make you strong?
sym1-07.pray: St. Peter, you knew weakness and grace. Pray for me, that the Spirit may make me faithful.
sym1-07.do: Do one thing today that takes a little courage for your faith: make the Sign of the Cross in public, or say you go to church.

sym1-07.title: The fruit of the Spirit
sym1-07.think: Paul lists twelve fruits of the Spirit: charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency and chastity. Fruit grows slowly, from a living root.
sym1-07.journal: Which fruit of the Spirit do you most want to grow in you?
sym1-07.pray: Holy Spirit, let your fruit grow in me today, especially patience and kindness.
sym1-07.do: Choose one fruit and practise it on purpose today with one person.

sym1-07.title: Bring your questions about grace
sym1-07.class: What do you want to ask about the Holy Spirit, grace, or how God works in us? Write it down.
sym1-07.think: "You have received the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry: Abba (Father)." Grace makes you not a servant but a child of God.
sym1-07.journal: How would you live differently today if you truly felt like God's child?
sym1-07.pray: Abba, Father, I am your child. Let your Spirit pray in me.
sym1-07.do: Practise the memory verse with the flashcards, and read your questions once more.

sym1-08.title: Upon this rock
sym1-08.think: Jesus did not leave a book and walk away. He gathered people, chose twelve, made Peter the rock, and promised that the gates of hell would not prevail. The Church is his idea.
sym1-08.journal: What did you think about "the Church" before RCIA? What do you think now?
sym1-08.pray: Lord Jesus, you built your Church on the rock. Thank you for bringing me to her. Make me a living stone.
sym1-08.do: Look up who the current Pope is and who your bishop is, and pray for them both by name.

sym1-08.title: The first Christian community
sym1-08.think: The first Christians "were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread, and in prayers." Teaching, Eucharist, community, prayer: the Church still lives on these four.
sym1-08.journal: Which of the four do you need most right now?
sym1-08.pray: Lord, make my parish a family like the first Christians, and help me to belong.
sym1-08.do: Do this week's Bible study on Acts 2:42-47.

sym1-08.title: Why be Catholic?

media.title: Fr. Mike: Why be Catholic?
media.about: Fr. Mike answers a common question: why not just love Jesus on my own? He explains that Jesus gave us the Church to give us himself, in the sacraments and in the teaching handed down from the apostles, and that faith is meant to be lived together.
media.listen: the difference between a club of believers and the Body of Christ.

sym1-08.think: "One body and one Spirit... one Lord, one faith, one baptism." Unity is not sameness; it is many members sharing one life.
sym1-08.journal: What gift do you bring to the Body of Christ?
sym1-08.pray: Lord, keep your Church one. Heal what divides Christians, and make me a peacemaker.
sym1-08.do: Learn the four marks of the Church from the Creed: one, holy, catholic and apostolic.

sym1-08.title: Jesus yes, Church no?

reason.q: Can't I just have Jesus without the Church?
steps: Jesus himself founded a community with leaders, rituals and a mission. Choosing Jesus means accepting what he chose.
We only know Jesus because the Church remembered him, wrote the New Testament, chose which books belong in it and handed it on to us.
Paul calls the Church the Body of Christ. A head without a body, or a hand cut off from the body, does not make sense.
Alone, our faith easily bends to our moods. Together, with the sacraments and the apostles' teaching, it is corrected, fed and carried when we are weak.

sym1-08.think: "If one member suffer any thing, all the members suffer with it." You need the Church, and the Church needs you.
sym1-08.journal: What has the Church community already given you this year?
sym1-08.pray: Lord, I am one part of your Body. Use me, and let me receive what others give.
sym1-08.do: Introduce yourself to one new person at Mass this Sunday.

sym1-08.title: He followed the evidence to Rome

story.name: St. John Henry Newman
story.text:
John Henry Newman was a famous Anglican priest and scholar at Oxford in the 1800s. He set out to prove that the Church of England was the true heir of the early Church, and he spent years reading the Church Fathers.

The more he studied, the more he saw the early Church in the Catholic Church. "To be deep in history is to cease to be Protestant," he wrote. In 1845, at the cost of his career and many friendships, he was received into the Catholic Church. He became a cardinal, and was declared a saint in 2019. His motto: "Heart speaks to heart."

sym1-08.think: Newman used his mind honestly and followed it where it led, even when it cost him. Reason and faith walked together.
sym1-08.journal: What is your journey into the Church costing you? What is it giving you?
sym1-08.pray: Lead, kindly Light, amid the encircling gloom, lead thou me on. I do not ask to see the distant scene; one step enough for me. (St. John Henry Newman)
sym1-08.do: Read about one Church Father (Ignatius of Antioch, Justin, Irenaeus) and notice what the early Christians believed about the Eucharist and bishops.

sym1-08.title: Belong to a parish
sym1-08.think: "Not forsaking our assembly, as some are accustomed." Sunday Mass is not just a duty; it is where the family gathers and is fed.
sym1-08.journal: What would help you feel more at home in your parish?
sym1-08.pray: Lord, bless my parish, our priest, our catechists and everyone in RCIA with me.
sym1-08.do: Pick up the parish bulletin this Sunday and find one group or event you could join.

sym1-08.title: Questions about the Church
sym1-08.class: What do you want to ask about the Church: the Pope, bishops, other Christians, the scandals, what "catholic" means? Write it down. Hard questions are welcome.
sym1-08.think: "I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world." Jesus promised to stay with his Church, through every century and every scandal.
sym1-08.journal: In one sentence: why do you want to become Catholic?
sym1-08.pray: Lord, you are with us always. Thank you for your Church, holy and full of sinners like me.
sym1-08.do: Read your journal from this week and add any question to your list.

sym1-09.title: Behold thy mother
sym1-09.think: From the cross Jesus gives his mother to the beloved disciple, and the disciple to her. The Church has always heard this as a gift to every disciple: Mary is our mother too.
sym1-09.journal: What do you feel about Mary right now: closeness, confusion, questions?
sym1-09.pray: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
sym1-09.do: Pray one Hail Mary slowly today, thinking about each phrase.

sym1-09.title: Be it done to me
sym1-09.think: Mary is young, poor, and confused ("How shall this be done?"), and she says yes. Her yes made room for God to become man. Every Christian life is a smaller yes like hers.
sym1-09.journal: What is God asking you to say yes to, even without understanding everything?
sym1-09.pray: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word. Mary, teach me your yes.
sym1-09.do: Do this week's Bible study on the Annunciation (Luke 1:26-38).

sym1-09.title: Why Catholics love Mary

media.title: Fr. Mike on Mary
media.about: Fr. Mike explains why Catholics honour Mary without worshipping her: everything about her points to Jesus. She is the Mother of God because her son is God, and she prays for us as a mother.
media.listen: the difference between worship (only God) and honour (Mary and the saints).

sym1-09.think: Mary says, "all generations shall call me blessed," and gives the reason: "he that is mighty hath done great things to me." Honouring Mary is praising what God did.
sym1-09.journal: What great things has God done for you? List three.
sym1-09.pray: My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
sym1-09.do: Read the whole Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), Mary's song, once aloud.

sym1-09.title: Do Catholics worship Mary?

reason.q: Isn't praying to Mary and the saints taking something from God?
steps: Catholics worship God alone. Worship means giving someone the honour due to God, and the Church has always condemned giving that to any creature.
Asking Mary to pray for us is like asking a friend to pray for us. Death does not end the family of God; the saints are alive in Christ.
At Cana, Mary notices the need and says to Jesus, "They have no wine," and to the servants, "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye." That is all she ever does: brings us to him.
Honouring a mother honours her son. Calling Mary "Mother of God" protects the truth that Jesus is God.

sym1-09.think: The first miracle happens because Mary asks. Jesus loves to answer his mother.
sym1-09.journal: What would you like Mary to bring to Jesus for you, like at Cana?
sym1-09.pray: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection was left unaided.
sym1-09.do: Ask Mary to pray for one specific need today, then leave it with Jesus.

sym1-09.title: A sceptic in a church in Rome

story.name: Alphonse Ratisbonne
story.text:
Alphonse Ratisbonne was a wealthy young banker from Strasbourg, from a Jewish family, and he openly mocked Christianity. In Rome in January 1842 a friend dared him to wear a Miraculous Medal of Mary and say the Memorare each day. He agreed, as a joke.

On January 20, waiting for that friend inside the church of Sant'Andrea delle Fratte, he suddenly saw Mary, full of light, who made a sign for him to kneel. "She did not say a word, but I understood everything," he wrote. Eleven days later he was baptized. He became a priest and spent his life in the Holy Land.

sym1-09.think: Alphonse did not go looking for God. A small prayer, said almost as a joke, opened a door. Never underestimate a little prayer.
sym1-09.journal: Is there someone you could quietly pray the Memorare for every day?
sym1-09.pray: Mary, Mother of Jesus, pray for all who do not yet know your Son, and for me.
sym1-09.do: Pray the Memorare today for someone far from faith.

sym1-09.title: A family in heaven
sym1-09.think: "We also having so great a cloud of witnesses over our head." The saints are like a stadium cheering us on. You will choose one of them as your patron for Confirmation.
sym1-09.journal: Which saint have you felt drawn to so far, and why?
sym1-09.pray: All you holy men and women, saints of God, pray for us.
sym1-09.do: Take the "Find my saint" quiz in the app, or read about two saints.

sym1-09.title: Questions about Mary and the saints
sym1-09.class: What do you want to ask about Mary, the saints, statues, relics or the Rosary? Write it down.
sym1-09.think: John sees "a woman clothed with the sun... and on her head a crown of twelve stars," who gives birth to a son. The Church sees Mary, and also the people of God.
sym1-09.journal: How has your view of Mary changed this week?
sym1-09.pray: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope.
sym1-09.do: Pray one decade of the Rosary in the app before class.

sym1-10.title: I am the resurrection
sym1-10.think: Martha has just buried her brother, and Jesus tells her: "I am the resurrection and the life." Then he asks, "Believest thou this?" The last things are not a scary topic; they are the question of hope.
sym1-10.journal: What do you feel when you think about your own death?
sym1-10.pray: Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life. I believe; help me to believe more.
sym1-10.do: Pray for someone you love who has died, by name.

sym1-10.title: Lazarus, come forth
sym1-10.think: "Jesus wept." He knows he will raise Lazarus, and still he weeps with his friends. God does not stand far from our grief.
sym1-10.journal: What grief do you want to bring to Jesus?
sym1-10.pray: Lord, you wept at your friend's grave. Weep with me, and call me out of every tomb.
sym1-10.do: Do this week's Bible study on John 11.

sym1-10.title: What the Church really teaches about purgatory

media.by: Bishop Robert Barron, Word on Fire
media.title: Bishop Barron on purgatory and heaven
media.about: Bishop Barron explains purgatory not as a punishment but as God's love finishing its work in us: a final purification so we can bear the full joy of heaven. It is good news for everyone who dies loving God but not yet perfect.
media.listen: the image of fire as love, not torture.

sym1-10.think: Paul says some will be saved "yet so as by fire." The Church sees here a hint of purification after death, and so we pray for the dead.
sym1-10.journal: What would you want God to purify in you?
sym1-10.pray: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace.
sym1-10.do: Add the names of your dead to "People I pray for" in the app.

sym1-10.title: Would a loving God send anyone to hell?

reason.q: How can a loving God allow hell?
steps: God made us free so we could love. Love cannot be forced. If we can say yes to God, we can also say a final no.
The Church teaches that hell is "self-exclusion" from God: not God's wish, but his respect for a person's final choice (Catechism 1033).
God "will have all men to be saved" and does everything to bring us home. No one ends up in hell by accident or by a mistake they did not choose.
The Church declares many people saints in heaven, but has never declared that any particular person is in hell. We hope and pray for everyone.

sym1-10.think: At the last judgment Jesus asks about simple things: food, water, a visit. Heaven grows from small acts of love now.
sym1-10.journal: What does this teaching make you feel, and what does it make you want to do?
sym1-10.pray: O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, lead all souls to heaven, especially those most in need of thy mercy.
sym1-10.do: Visit, call or help one person who is sick, lonely or in need this week.

sym1-10.title: Lay this body anywhere

story.name: St. Monica
story.text:
Monica lived in North Africa in the 300s. Her husband had a hard temper, and her son Augustine lived far from God. For seventeen years she prayed and wept for him. A bishop told her, "The son of so many tears cannot perish."

She lived to see Augustine baptized. On the way home from Italy, at the port of Ostia, she fell ill. Her sons wanted to bury her in Africa beside her husband. She said, "Lay this body anywhere; do not let care for it trouble you. This only I ask: that you remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you are."

sym1-10.think: Monica was not afraid of where she died, because she knew where she was going. She asked only to be prayed for at Mass.
sym1-10.journal: Whom do you want to remember at the altar? Write their names.
sym1-10.pray: St. Monica, pray for all mothers and fathers waiting for their children to come home to God.
sym1-10.do: At Mass this Sunday, silently offer the Mass for someone who has died.

sym1-10.title: Live today for heaven
sym1-10.think: Paul forgets what is behind and stretches toward what is ahead, because "our conversation is in heaven." Thinking about heaven does not take us out of the world; it shows what matters in it.
sym1-10.journal: If you had one month to live, what would you change?
sym1-10.pray: Lord, teach me to number my days, that I may gain a wise heart.
sym1-10.do: Pray the Evening Examen tonight: look back over the day with God.

sym1-10.title: Questions about the end
sym1-10.class: What do you want to ask about death, judgment, heaven, hell, purgatory or the end of the world? Write it down.
sym1-10.think: "God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: and death shall be no more." The Bible ends not with destruction but with a wedding and a new creation.
sym1-10.journal: What are you most looking forward to in heaven?
sym1-10.pray: Behold, I make all things new. Lord, make me new, and bring us all home.
sym1-10.do: Read your questions once more. This is the end of the first part of Symbolon.

sym2-01.title: Born of water and the Spirit
sym2-01.think: Nicodemus comes at night with questions, and Jesus says one must be "born again of water and the Holy Ghost." Baptism is not a symbol only; it is a new birth into God's family.
sym2-01.journal: If you are not yet baptized: what do you hope Baptism will change? If you are: what do you know about your own baptism?
sym2-01.pray: Lord, like Nicodemus I come with questions. Give me new birth by water and the Spirit.
sym2-01.do: Use holy water when you enter church this Sunday and make the Sign of the Cross, remembering Baptism.

sym2-01.title: Buried and risen with Christ
sym2-01.think: "We are buried together with him by baptism into death," so that we may walk in newness of life. Going down into the water is dying with Christ; coming up is rising with him.
sym2-01.journal: What in your old life do you want to leave in the water?
sym2-01.pray: Jesus, I want to die with you to sin and rise with you to new life.
sym2-01.do: Do this week's Bible study on John 3:1-17.

sym2-01.title: Sealed with the Spirit

media.title: Bishop Barron on the Sacrament of Confirmation
media.about: A ten-minute sermon. Bishop Barron explains that Confirmation completes Baptism: it seals us with the Holy Spirit and sends us out on mission, like soldiers or athletes who are strengthened for a task, not just blessed.
media.listen: what the Spirit gives you for, not only what he gives you.

sym2-01.think: Peter and John lay hands on the new Christians in Samaria, "and they received the Holy Ghost." The bishop still does this at Confirmation, and in RCIA the priest does it at the Easter Vigil.
sym2-01.journal: For what mission might God be strengthening you?
sym2-01.pray: Be sealed with the gift of the Holy Spirit. Come, Holy Spirit, and make me ready.
sym2-01.do: Start thinking about your Confirmation name: a saint you would like as a friend for life.

sym2-01.title: Why be baptized if I already believe?

reason.q: Isn't faith in my heart enough?
steps: Jesus himself commanded Baptism: "Teach ye all nations, baptizing them." Wanting Jesus includes wanting what he asked.
We are body and soul. God gives grace through things we can see and touch (water, oil, bread) because that is how human beings receive gifts.
Baptism is not a reward for believing; it is God's action. It forgives all sin, makes us children of God, and joins us to the Church.
Love wants to be public, like a wedding. Baptism is your yes to God said aloud, in front of his family.

sym2-01.think: When the crowd asked, "What shall we do?", Peter answered: "Do penance, and be baptized every one of you." About three thousand did, that same day.
sym2-01.journal: What makes you want to be baptized or confirmed, in your own words?
sym2-01.pray: Lord, I want to belong to you completely, in body and soul, in front of your Church.
sym2-01.do: Write a short letter to God about why you want the sacraments. Keep it for the Easter Vigil.

sym2-01.title: The Lily of the Mohawks

story.name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
story.text:
Kateri was born in 1656 in a Mohawk village in what is now New York State. Smallpox killed her parents and left her face scarred and her eyes weak. She heard about Jesus from Jesuit missionaries and longed to be baptized, though her family opposed it.

She was baptized at 20, on Easter Sunday 1676, and was mocked and threatened for her faith. She walked some 300 kilometres to the Christian mission at Kahnawake, near Montreal, where she lived a life of prayer and care for others. She died at 24, and her scars are said to have faded. She was the first Indigenous saint of North America.

sym2-01.think: Kateri's baptism cost her a lot, and she never regretted it. She is buried in Kahnawake, in Quebec, where pilgrims still visit her.
sym2-01.journal: What has your journey to the sacraments already cost you, and has it been worth it?
sym2-01.pray: St. Kateri, you longed for Baptism. Pray for me and for all the catechumens in Canada.
sym2-01.do: Pray for the others in your RCIA group by name today.

sym2-01.title: Clothed in Christ
sym2-01.think: "As many of you as have been baptized in Christ, have put on Christ." At Baptism you receive a white garment. Every day after, you put him on again: in how you speak, choose and love.
sym2-01.journal: How would you like people to see Christ in you?
sym2-01.pray: Lord, as I get dressed today, clothe me with your kindness, patience and joy.
sym2-01.do: Each time you get dressed today, say: "Jesus, I put you on."

sym2-01.title: Questions about Baptism and Confirmation
sym2-01.class: What do you want to know about the Easter Vigil, your baptism, a sponsor, your Confirmation name or being received if already baptized? Write it down.
sym2-01.think: "I will pour upon you clean water... and I will give you a new heart." Ezekiel's promise is fulfilled in Baptism.
sym2-01.journal: Which promise of God from this week do you want to hold on to?
sym2-01.pray: I believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord.
sym2-01.do: Look at the rites ahead in the app: when will you receive the sacraments?

sym2-02.title: The bread of life
sym2-02.think: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger." In class you heard that in the Eucharist Jesus gives us himself, really, under the appearance of bread and wine.
sym2-02.journal: What are you hungry for, deep down?
sym2-02.pray: Jesus, bread of life, I hunger for you. Feed me with yourself.
sym2-02.do: At Mass this Sunday, watch closely when the priest lifts the Host and says, "This is my Body."

sym2-02.title: My flesh is meat indeed
sym2-02.think: Jesus does not soften his words when people object. He repeats them more strongly: "my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed." Many walk away. He lets them go rather than say it is only a symbol.
sym2-02.journal: If Jesus is truly present in the Eucharist, what does that change for you?
sym2-02.pray: O Sacrament most holy, O Sacrament divine, all praise and all thanksgiving be every moment thine.
sym2-02.do: Do this week's Bible study on John 6:35-69.

sym2-02.title: The Real Presence

media.title: The Real Presence of Jesus in the Eucharist
media.about: A full talk. Bishop Barron explains from John 6, the Last Supper and the early Church why Catholics believe the Eucharist is not a symbol of Jesus but Jesus himself, and why it matters that many Catholics rediscover this.
media.listen: what Paul means by "not discerning the body of the Lord."

sym2-02.think: Paul wrote this only about twenty-five years after the Last Supper. Already the Church believed that eating unworthily is sinning "against the body and blood of the Lord."
sym2-02.journal: How do you want to prepare for your First Communion?
sym2-02.pray: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.
sym2-02.do: Watch the first part of the talk, or read the summary, then read 1 Corinthians 11 again.

sym2-02.title: How can bread become God?

reason.q: Isn't it irrational to believe bread becomes Jesus?
steps: The Church distinguishes what a thing is (its substance) from how it appears (its colour, taste, shape). After the consecration, the appearances of bread remain, but what it is has changed.
This is not magic or a chemical change you could test. It is God, who made bread from nothing, acting on what bread is.
Jesus said "This is my body," not "This represents." The earliest Christians, like St. Ignatius of Antioch around 107, wrote plainly that the Eucharist is the flesh of Jesus.
If God could become a man in Mary's womb, he can give himself to us under the form of bread. The question is not "can he?" but "did he say so?" He did.

sym2-02.think: At the Last Supper, Jesus took bread and said, "This is my body, which is given for you." The next day he gave that body on the cross.
sym2-02.journal: What part of this teaching is hardest for you to accept, and why?
sym2-02.pray: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief. Let me see you in the breaking of the bread.
sym2-02.do: Find out when your parish has Eucharistic Adoration and plan to go for fifteen minutes.

sym2-02.title: The highway to heaven

story.name: St. Carlo Acutis
story.text:
Carlo Acutis was an ordinary Italian teenager who loved video games, football and computers. He also went to Mass every day after his First Communion at seven, and spent time before the Blessed Sacrament. "The Eucharist is my highway to heaven," he said.

He taught himself to code and built a website documenting Eucharistic miracles around the world, which is still used today. In 2006, at fifteen, he died of leukaemia, offering his suffering for the Pope and the Church. He was declared a saint in 2025, the first saint of the internet generation.

sym2-02.think: "O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet." Carlo was not unusual in his interests. He was unusual in letting Jesus be the centre of them.
sym2-02.journal: How could your phone, your work or your hobby point to Jesus?
sym2-02.pray: St. Carlo Acutis, pray for me, that the Eucharist may become my highway to heaven too.
sym2-02.do: Spend fifteen minutes in a church, near the tabernacle, if you can this week.

sym2-02.title: Spiritual communion
sym2-02.think: Zacchaeus could not get close to Jesus, so he climbed a tree. Jesus saw him and said, "this day I must abide in thy house." Until you can receive Communion, you can still invite him in your heart.
sym2-02.journal: What does it feel like to wait for Communion?
sym2-02.pray: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. Since I cannot now receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart.
sym2-02.do: At Communion time this Sunday, if you are not yet receiving, pray this spiritual communion in your seat, or come forward for a blessing with arms crossed.

sym2-02.title: Questions about the Eucharist
sym2-02.class: What do you want to ask about the Eucharist, Communion, Adoration, or why non-Catholics do not receive? Write it down.
sym2-02.think: When many leave, Jesus asks the twelve, "Will you also go away?" Peter answers: "Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life."
sym2-02.journal: Write Peter's answer as your own prayer.
sym2-02.pray: Lord, to whom shall I go? You have the words of eternal life.
sym2-02.do: Practise the memory verse and read your questions once more.

sym2-03.title: Do this in memory of me
sym2-03.think: The Mass has two great parts: the Liturgy of the Word, where God speaks, and the Liturgy of the Eucharist, where Jesus gives himself. It is the same pattern as Emmaus: Scripture, then the breaking of bread.
sym2-03.journal: Which part of the Mass do you understand better now, after class?
sym2-03.pray: Lord Jesus, you gave us the Mass so we would never forget you. Help me to take part with my whole heart.
sym2-03.do: Open the Mass guide in the app and read the parts you still find confusing.

sym2-03.title: The Mass in the Bible
sym2-03.think: Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne and angels crying "Holy, holy, holy." At every Mass, just before the Eucharistic Prayer, we sing the same words, joining the angels.
sym2-03.journal: Have you ever felt something holy at Mass? What was it like?
sym2-03.pray: Holy, holy, holy Lord God of hosts. Heaven and earth are full of your glory. Hosanna in the highest.
sym2-03.do: Do this week's Bible study on Luke 22:14-20.

sym2-03.title: What happens at Mass

media.by: Bishop Robert Barron, Word on Fire
media.title: Bishop Barron on the Mass
media.about: Bishop Barron walks through the Mass as a journey: we gather, confess, listen, offer, are fed and are sent. He shows how each part has roots in the Bible and why the Mass is the most important thing Catholics do.
media.listen: why the end of Mass, "Go forth," matters as much as the beginning.

sym2-03.think: At Mass "you are come to mount Sion... and to the company of many thousands of angels." Your small parish church on a Sunday morning touches heaven.
sym2-03.journal: What would help you pay attention at Mass?
sym2-03.pray: Lord, open my eyes at Mass to see heaven touching earth.
sym2-03.do: Read this Sunday's readings before Mass on Living with Christ, so you arrive ready to listen.

sym2-03.title: Why every Sunday?

reason.q: Can't I pray at home instead of going to Mass?
steps: Prayer at home is good, but the Mass is something else: it is Jesus' own sacrifice made present, which no private prayer can replace.
